## Summary

Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.

Fix the parser before merge because `--json --junit junit.xml` fails when it should produce both reports.

## Changes

The pull request adds `--json` with an optional path and a default of `results.json`. It also adds a helper that writes reports to the parsed destinations.

## Critical

- app/cli.py:15 — correctness — Stop `--json` from consuming the next flag — With `--json --junit junit.xml`, the parser takes `--junit` as the JSON path and rejects `junit.xml` as an unknown option. — Users who put `--json` before `--junit` and omit the JSON path get neither report. — Fix: Use the `--junit` branch’s `startswith("--")` check to detect the next option and leave it for the parser.

## Important

- app/cli.py:30 — correctness — Reject a shared JSON and JUnit destination — With `--junit report.xml --json report.xml`, `write_reports` succeeds after the second write replaces the JUnit XML with JSON. — When both options name the same file, downstream JUnit consumers cannot read the requested test results. — Fix: Check that the destinations resolve to distinct paths before writing either report.

## Suggestions

- app/cli.py:29 — tests — Test writing JSON and JUnit together — No test exercises the writer’s second iteration for `--junit junit.xml --json report.json`. The JSON test writes one file, and the JUnit test only parses arguments. — A regression that skips the second write could pass the tests while dropping JSON from a valid two-report invocation.
